chapters.title: Arjuna's Despair
chapters.description: Arjuna is on the battlefield, ready to fight a war against his own family and teachers. He is overcome with sadness and confusion about what is right. This sets the stage for a conversation about life and duty.

chapters.title: The Path of Knowledge
chapters.description: Krishna explains that the soul never dies; only the physical body does. He introduces the core lesson of the text: do your duty simply because it is the right thing to do, without worrying about the reward or the final result.

chapters.title: The Path of Action
chapters.description: Everyone has to take action in life. The secret to freedom is to act selflessly. When you do your work to help others and fulfill your responsibilities instead of acting out of greed, you free yourself from stress and karma.

chapters.title: Knowledge and Action
chapters.description: Krishna explains that he appears on earth whenever goodness is in danger. He teaches that when you truly understand how the universe works, you realize that doing selfless work is the exact same thing as living a holy, dedicated life.

chapters.title: True Renunciation
chapters.description: Arjuna asks if it is better to leave society behind or to stay and work in the world. Krishna answers that while both paths work, staying in the world and doing your duty without being attached to the results is the better and more practical choice.

chapters.title: The Path of Meditation
chapters.description: Krishna teaches how to calm a busy and restless mind. By practicing meditation, controlling your desires, and focusing inward, you can find lasting peace and see the divine presence in everything.

chapters.title: Knowledge of the Divine
chapters.description: Krishna explains that everything in the universe, both physical matter and spiritual energy, comes from him. He describes the different types of people who search for spiritual truth and why they do it.

chapters.title: The Eternal Spirit
chapters.description: This chapter focuses on the end of life. Krishna explains that your state of mind at the exact moment of death determines what happens to you next. Remembering the divine at the end leads to ultimate freedom.

chapters.title: The Supreme Secret
chapters.description: Krishna reveals the power of pure love and devotion. He explains that anyone, no matter their background or past mistakes, can find ultimate peace by offering whatever they do to the divine with a loving heart.

chapters.title: Divine Glories
chapters.description: To build Arjuna's confidence, Krishna describes his endless power. He explains that everything beautiful, strong, wise, and amazing in the world is just a tiny spark of his own brilliance.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Vision
chapters.description: Krishna grants Arjuna a special vision to see his universal form. Arjuna is awestruck and terrified to see the entire universe, including all creation and destruction, contained within Krishna.

chapters.title: The Path of Devotion
chapters.description: Krishna explains that loving devotion is the easiest and most direct way to reach spiritual perfection. He lists the qualities of a person who truly loves the divine, such as being kind, forgiving, and peaceful.

chapters.title: Body and Soul
chapters.description: This chapter separates our physical body from our inner consciousness. It explains how the pure soul gets tangled up in the material world and teaches how to clearly see the difference between the two.

chapters.title: The Three Qualities of Nature
chapters.description: Krishna explains that all human behavior is driven by three natural forces: goodness, passion, and ignorance. To be truly free and at peace, a person must learn to rise above all three of these forces.

chapters.title: The Supreme Person
chapters.description: Krishna uses the picture of an upside-down tree to represent the material world. He teaches that we must cut down this tree of worldly attachment to reach our true, eternal spiritual home.

chapters.title: Divine and Demonic Traits
chapters.description: This chapter lists the qualities that live inside humans. Divine traits like honesty, harmlessness, and courage lead to freedom. Demonic traits like anger, greed, and arrogance lead to suffering.

chapters.title: Three Kinds of Faith
chapters.description: Krishna explains that our natural personality shapes our faith, the food we prefer, the charity we give, and our daily habits. Everything we do is colored by either goodness, passion, or ignorance.

chapters.title: Liberation and Surrender
chapters.description: In this final summary, Krishna concludes that true sacrifice does not mean stopping your work, but stopping your selfish desire for a reward. His ultimate advice is to let go of all worries and simply surrender to the divine with complete love.
